articles.title: Amani Hooker Traded to Bills, Titans' NFL Draft Pick Return Revealed After Deadline Deal
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills bolstered their defense ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills bolstered their defense ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.

Buffalo acquired safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick from the Tennessee Titans in exchange for a second-round draft pick.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero and ESPN's Adam Schefter first reported the deal.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that prior to dealing for Hooker, the Bills "made a very strong push" for Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker.

A 2019 fourth-round pick, Hooker had spent his entire career in Tennessee. His fellow draft classmate Jeffery Simmons was also shipped away this season, with the Titans sending the standout defensive tackle to the Chicago Bears.

Hooker is tied for the league lead with five interceptions this year, giving him 17 picks for his career. He's also added 52 total tackles and six passes defended this season.

Hooker is an immediate upgrade for the Bills, who have a combined total of six interceptions through eight games. Buffalo added veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson over the offseason, but his disappointing tenure included a one-game suspension and subpar play before he was released earlier this month. If Hooker lives up to expectations, he could be the missing piece that puts the team over the top as title contenders.

The Bills already appear to be the favorites to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, improving to 7-1 with a 23-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football . Buffalo's struggling defense has benefited from facing backup quarterbacks in back-to-back weeks, and it will have another easy outing on Sunday against the 2-7 New York Jets.

articles.title: Josh Downs is latest Colt to be dealt at NFL trade deadline; here's what we know
articles.summary: Josh Downs is the latest Colts to be traded, joining Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner and Keenan Allen. Did they get enough? What's the receiver depth chart?
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — Josh Downs got what he wanted in the end.

Indianapolis has dealt Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs with a 2027 seventh-round pick for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks in the final hour before the NFL trade deadline, according to reports, granting the slot receiver's request for a deal.

Downs requested a trade shortly after the team decided to deal left guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, and he openly acknowledged that he was comfortable with the idea of playing elsewhere.

"I'm open to whatever comes my way," Downs said at the time.

See Colts receiver Josh Downs through the years

The slot receiver's performance since he made the trade request has been erratic, matching a disappointing season for the fourth-year player overall.

Downs has caught 33 passes for 354 yards and a touchdown this season, failing to live to former general manager Chris Ballard's predictions that he would take advantage of the opportunity opened by trading Michael Pittman Jr. this offseason.

Opponents have frequently double-teamed Downs in the absence of Alec Pierce.

Downs hasn't been able to regularly beat those coverages, and he has played a key role in each of the team's last two home losses.

Downs dropped three key passes in the team's shocking loss to the Titans , the game that precipitated Ballard's firing and set the wheels in motion for the team's rebuild, and on Sunday, he dropped two more passes, including a third-down throw that could have allowed Indianapolis to play for the game-winning field goal without giving the ball back to the Cowboys at all.

"I stunk today, but it's the game of football sometimes. I didn't catch those passes when I should have, and that's that," Downs said after Sunday's loss. "I dropped a couple against Tennessee as well. I don't really know what it was. I just gotta focus on the ball, make a couple good catches. I dropped simple ones."

Downs' future in Indianapolis was already cloudy.

Drafted in the third round in 2023, Downs has 231 catches for 2,494 yards and 12 touchdowns in three and a half years as a Colt. Before the season, there were questions about whether the Colts would sign Downs to an extension, but he pushed back on the idea that he was seeking an extension in Indianapolis coming into the season.

"If it came my way, it came my way, but I wouldn't say that," Downs said.

When the Colts traded Nelson and Buckner to the Seahawks and 49ers, respectively, the franchise indicated that they were willing to deal almost any piece in exchange for future assets. Indianapolis also traded veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen to San Francisco for a sixth-round pick on Tuesday.

The moves sent a message to the rest of the NFL that the Colts are entering a deep rebuild, the kind that will leave the team out of competition for a couple of seasons.

It also sent a message that any player in the locker room might be available.

For weeks now, Downs has sounded like a man comfortable with the possibility of change.

"It is what it is," Downs said. "I'm here today, but whatever comes my way, comes my way, and I'll go from there."

He gets the change of scenery he wanted.

The Colts take another step into the future.

Joel A. Erickson and Nathan Brown cover the Colts all season. Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Colts Insider newsletter .

articles.title: Josh Downs: Patrick Mahomes gets new weapon as Kansas City Chiefs trade for wide receiver
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have acquired Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts; Wide receiver is an area of need for the Chiefs and Downs had requested a trade; Downs has 33 passes for 354 yards and a touchdown this season
articles.body:
The Chiefs will also receive a seventh-round pick for the 2027 season, while the Colts will receive a fourth-round selection and fifth-round selection for 2027.

It was reported in late October that Downs has requested a trade and now his wish has come to fruition.

It means the Chiefs have filled their biggest position of need just two days after Xavier Worthy sustained a hamstring injury in their win over the Jets.

The Chiefs lost their top deep threat, Tyquan Thornton, to a potentially season-ending fractured ankle a few weeks ago. Fellow wide receiver Rashee Rice has been prone to injury, missing three games this season to a hamstring injury, while Worthy could miss several weeks after grabbing at his hamstring in the second half of a 35-12 rout of New York on Sunday.

Downs has 33 passes for 354 yards and a touchdown this season and offers a vital playmaking option at wide receiver for the Chiefs and Mahomes.

He is not the only Colts receiver who has been traded after Keenan Allen went to the San Francisco 49ers.

Downs was himself a third-round pick back in 2023.

After the Colts' loss to the Cowboys on Sunday, Downs said: "I said I'm open to whatever, and if they want me to stay here, I'm going to stay here.

"And if they don't, if they want to trade me away, they'll trade me away."

articles.title: Tony Pollard Reportedly Not Traded by Titans After NFL Deadline Rumors
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans are holding on to one of the team's most valuable trade chips despite a 1-7 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans are holding on to one of the team's most valuable trade chips despite a 1-7 start to the 2026 season.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Tuesday the Titans are planning to keep running back Tony Pollard past the 4 p.m. ET deadline after receiving interest from other teams.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the Denver Broncos and New York Giants were among teams interested in Pollard before the deadline.

Pollard has led the Titans this season with 595 rushing yards and six touchdowns in eight games.

The 29-year-old went into the 2026 campaign on the final year of his previous three-year, $21.75 million deal with the Titans.

Pollard is riding a streak of five straight campaigns with at least 1,000 rushing yards dating back to his tenure with the Dallas Cowboys.

The Titans signed Pollard, who spent the first five seasons of his NFL career with the Cowboys, in free agency ahead of the 2024 season.

Pollard's future with the Titans was brought into question by some analysts around the 2026 NFL draft, ahead of which some mocks projected the Titans targeting a running back.

The Titans instead drafted wide receiver Carnell Tate at No. 4, keeping Pollard on track to continue serving as the team's lead back going forward.

The lack of movement at the deadline could be seen as a sign the Titans hope to extend Pollard as a long-term piece of an offense looking to take a step forward in Cam Ward's third season.

With Pollard leading the running back room and Tate continuing to develop, head coach Robert Saleh will hope to surround Ward with a stronger offense in 2027.

articles.title: From Kirk Cousins saving Vikings' defense to Chargers ignoring reality, NFL trade deadline winners and losers
articles.summary: Many in Minnesota win with Cousins' arrival. Justin Jefferson no doubt is breathing a little more easily after the news. Meanwhile, the Chargers' passivity i...
articles.body:
The NFL schedule makers scored a win with their pre-trade deadline "Monday Night Football" matchup.

Pitting two of the league's top teams against each other meant two teams likely to be active at the deadline would meet on national television to expose each other's vulnerabilities.

The Buffalo Bills' 23-6 takedown of the Minnesota Vikings did just that. And while Carson Wentz was starting in relief of an injured Kyler Murray (hamstring), the latest iteration of a toothless Minnesota offense alongside a menacing but asked-to-be-on-the-field-40-minutes Vikings defense signaled that change was necessary.

With less than 90 minutes remaining before the trade deadline, the Vikings dealt their 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for reuniting with quarterback Kirk Cousins , a person with knowledge of the deal confirmed to Yahoo Sports.

What does this mean for the state of the NFC North and the NFC's Super Bowl race generally? And what has the trade landscape leading up to the deadline done to change teams' fortunes?

Here are Yahoo Sports' winners and losers of the NFL trade deadline:

The Vikings' defense: Many in Minnesota win with Cousins' arrival. Receiver Justin Jefferson no doubt is breathing a little more easily after the news. But the Vikings' defense coordinated by Brian Flores has to be the biggest winner. Flores' unit has allowed the fewest points and second-fewest yards across the entire NFL this season. Minnesota's offense has rewarded the blitz-happy dominance with … the 27th-ranked scoring offense and 31st-ranked (that's second-worst, for those counting at home) total offense. Cousins arrives with 2,340 passing yards (fifth) and a 97.1 passer rating (11th) this season. He led the Raiders to an offense averaging 8.1 more points and 64.2 more yards per game this season. Cousins knows O'Connell's offense from their 2022 and 2023 partnership in Minnesota, giving him a "low start-up cost," in the words of one high-ranking AFC executive. At 6-2, the Vikings' chances of winning a crowded NFC North live.

The Rams' 'F them picks' strategy staying relevant: The Los Angeles Rams famously sacrificed the future for their present en route to the 2021 NFL season's Super Bowl. They earned an "F them picks" reputation for bucking traditional wisdom, and they continued to prioritize proven stars over picks this summer when they sent the Browns Jared Verse alongside a 2027 first-, 2028 second- and 2029 third-round pick to acquire reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett in June. The relevance now? Jacksonville Jaguars general manager James Gladstone came up in this league with the Rams and Los Angeles GM Les Snead. He has leaned into the ethos dating back to his first draft as GM, when he traded up for Travis Hunter, and he leaned into it again on Monday when he collected three new defensive players in one day — including two at steep prices .

The Jaguars aren't afraid to hamper their future to chase their window this year. So they sent the Eagles a 2027 first- and 2029 second-round pick for defensive tackle Jordan Davis; the Falcons a 2027 second- and 2028 fifth-round pick for safety Jessie Bates III; and the Saints a sixth-round pick (either 2027 or 2028, based on conditions) for defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. In Southern California, Snead was smiling.

Defensive tackles in vogue: Jeffery Simmons is not your average defensive tackle. But when the Chicago Bears became the first team in the modern draft era (since 1967) to pay two first-round picks for an interior defensive lineman, per ESPN research , the position received a well-deserved facelift. The Jaguars have since acquired two defensive tackles of their own, including a first-round pick in the deal for Davis. All of this comes in the shadows of the Cowboys paying big for Quinnen Williams at last year's deadline and the Cincinnati Bengals dealing the 10th overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft for Dexter Lawrence II. Just as Christian McCaffrey and Saquon Barkley once reasserted running backs' place relative to receivers in a pass-happy NFL era, consider this the defensive tackle reassertion relative to edge rushers. Offenses can't stand when interior linemen blow up the pocket, the protection challenges far dicier than blocking for a talented edge rusher. Defensive tackles are also hard to find — and often better once seasoned by a few years in the NFL.

"Everybody wants a quarterback and if you don't have a quarterback, what's the best way you can impact a quarterback? By that middle pressure and interior line movement …" an AFC executive said Monday by phone. "When you get a good one — man, just like when you get a good quarterback, you try to keep them as long as you can or they don't come to the market."

The Chiefs' passing game: For three straight games now, no Chiefs receiver has hit 55 receiving yards. Injuries play a role, but the ceiling of Patrick Mahomes and Co.'s offense nonetheless needed more than 37-year-old Travis Kelce and superhuman running back Kenneth Walker III manufacturing a passing game. Acquiring Colts receiver Josh Downs at the deadline , the Chiefs give themselves more depth even if not a drastically higher ceiling. Trading 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks for Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick wasn't cheap relative to Downs' recent play. But consider that the Pittsburgh Steelers and San Francisco 49ers (and arguably the Los Angeles Rams) also needed a receiver, and the Chiefs paying a fourth and change to close the deal makes sense. Can Kansas City now catch the Denver Broncos in the AFC West?

The Titans' negotiating chops: Tennessee already impressed with its ability to net two first-round picks for Simmons. Then, on Tuesday afternoon before the deadline, the Titans traded safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick to the Buffalo Bills for a second-round pick , per multiple reports. The Jessie Bates III deal likely outlined the parameters for the deal, and Hooker's league-best five interceptions for 114 yards this year helped. But the price was still rich for a player who hasn't been at the top of his position most of his career. Tennessee leveraged well the Bills' desire to keep pace in the AFC arms race.

Veteran Colts players wanting to win: A year ago, after nine games, the Colts were 7-2. This year: 2-7. They've already fired general manager Chris Ballard and are going nowhere this season. So godspeed to the two veterans on expiring contracts that were dealt with contenders. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner reunited with the San Francisco 49ers club that drafted him in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick. Three-time All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson joined the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks for a 2027 third- and 2028 fifth-round pick. The 49ers are a near lock to make the playoffs, at a 96% chance, per Next Gen Stats. The Seahawks face a more uphill battle in a tight division and conference, but Nelson's chance at competing is far greater than with Indianapolis. Each player earned more meaningful football with the trade; and the Colts, who were unlikely to re-sign either player when their contract expired in the spring, recouped draft capital and salary cap space.

The Eagles' quiet rebuild: Philadelphia had little choice but to trade receiver A.J. Brown in the offseason after he publicly made clear he wanted out and wasn't going to fall in line with quarterback Jalen Hurts. That haul — a 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fifth — began the Eagles' reset of cap space and draft capital as they pivot off an aging Super Bowl roster. The Eagles could have been more competitive this year if a rash of injuries, most notably blood clots in Hurts' lungs, didn't strike. But the injury-squandered year timed well with a retooling of resources for a roster that had been bursting at the seams. The Eagles have also since collected a 2028 second-round pick (with a fifth/seventh swap) for center Cam Jurgens as well as a 2027 first- and 2029 second-round pick for defensive tackle Jordan Davis. Adding two firsts and two seconds since June gives Philadelphia flexibility to build.

AFC South quarterbacks not named Trevor Lawrence: Monday was a rough day for C.J. Stroud, Daniel Jones and Cam Ward. The 6-2 Jaguars already hold double the number of wins as their nearest division foe (the Houston Texans are 3-5), and then they stockpiled Davis, Godchaux and Bates. Expect offenses to face more pressure at the line of scrimmage and more risk of turnovers against the Jaguars now: In his nine games with the Atlanta Falcons this season, Bates secured one interception, deflected four passes, forced three fumbles and returned one fumble for a touchdown. The Jaguars' 2027 second- and 2028 fifth-round picks were rich for a ninth-year player with half a year left on his contract. But Bates' play, and his veteran leadership in the secondary, will elevate the Jaguars' defensive ceiling into at least January.

Kevin O'Connell's QB whisperer reputation: Winning 64.5% of games in five years, and engineering multiple top-10 offenses, the Minnesota Vikings' Kevin O'Connell has proven he's a valuable head coach and play-caller. But two years ago, after Sam Darnold's resurgence in Minnesota, O'Connell was riding a reputation as a quarterback whisperer who would elevate and maximize any quarterback in his system. That luster has dimmed as the Vikings come off their third game this season without a touchdown. Minnesota thought it would spark Kyler Murray after acquiring the former No. 1 overall draft pick this spring, and he's instead currently 20th in passer rating as well as in and out of the lineup because of injury. Former second overall pick Carson Wentz played well last season in relief for Minnesota, but he has fallen off a cliff this year — most recently completing 32% of his pass attempts for 81 yards, two interceptions and a lost fumble in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday. And while it's disingenuous to say J.J. McCarthy would have solved the Vikings' QB woes in-house — some players simply need a change of scenery to find their footing, as McCarthy has with the Giants — Minnesota trading away a former first-round pick on his rookie deal for a fifth-round pick doesn't help perception as the club struggles to find an answer at the position. Perhaps a deep playoff run with Cousins will boost O'Connell's reputation in other areas.

The Colts' belief in Jonathan Taylor's market: Trading Buckner and Nelson never guaranteed the Colts would trade Jonathan Taylor. The prior two were veterans on expiring contracts; Taylor signed an extension in August and offers possible value for the 2027 Colts and beyond no matter who's coaching. So this loser column placement isn't to suggest the Colts should have dealt Taylor. But the Colts seemingly broadcasting their desired market for him appears to have backfired. League sources were well aware that Indianapolis wanted a Christian McCaffrey-like haul for Taylor: the equivalent of a 2027 second-, third- and fourth-round pick as well as a 2028 fifth-round pick. That was richer than any team could justify, so Taylor stays home. Was there a quieter way to go about this exploration, that put Taylor in less of an awkward position? "You play every game like it's your last …" Taylor said from his locker Sunday. "This place helped shape me into the man I am today, so I'm very grateful. So if it is, I'm very grateful for the city of Indianapolis." Narrator: It was not.

Brian Thomas Jr. fantasy managers: The Jaguars kept Thomas even as he averages 2.75 targets per game while seeing the field on just 43% of offensive snaps. The move means Thomas doesn't get the fresh start many believe would benefit him and likely doesn't get the on-field opportunities a team like the Kansas City Chiefs might have given him. A loss for Thomas and his fantasy managers, but a logical move according to league sources. Why? 1) Thomas' field-stretching ability opens up opportunities for his teammates in ways that could be hard to replicate without a player of his height, weight and especially speed. 2) If the Jaguars suffer an injury at the position, was a future draft pick worth a sudden weakness on the road to what the Jaguars believe can be the Super Bowl? And 3) The teams whose need was most likely to translate to strong pay for Thomas were the Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers. Would Jacksonville regret that during the AFC playoff bracket?

Jerry Jones' penchant for optimism: When the Cowboys were 2-4, team owner and general manager Jerry Jones was still optimistic enough to trumpet that "I would be active if we could get a chance to help the team this year." He still believed then in his offense's strength and his defense's capacity to improve. By this week, that optimism had faltered — not only because the Cowboys still sit beneath .500 at 4-5 but also because their last two performances against the Cardinals (an overtime loss) and the Colts (a narrow win) showed the Cowboys are playing more like the worst teams in the league than the best. "Overall," Jones told Dallas radio station 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday morning, "we're not playing very good." Could Dallas still make a run in a poor division? It's possible, with Next Gen Stats pitting their playoff chances at 31%. But paying handsomely for a player to help a year when the Cowboys look far behind the 49ers and entire NFC North wasn't wise. Not to mention the Cowboys already dealt a 2027 sixth- and 2028 second-round pick for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a contract year. Consider this week's patience a win for Jones' judgment, even if a loss for his unfailing optimism.

Fernando Mendoza's starting stretch: The 2026 first overall draft pick, Fernando Mendoza has already received more time to learn in the NFL than many rookie quarterbacks thrust into talent-shallow systems from the first week of their pro careers. In an ideal world, the Raiders would have given Mendoza still another month before starting. But receiving a third-round pick for Cousins was worth expediting Mendoza's timeline. Why a month? The Raiders face three tough defenses up next in the Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns. After their bye, the schedule lightens to the Los Angeles Chargers, a second Broncos matchup, the Titans, Arizona Cardinals and a likely-resting-their-starters Chiefs team. Mendoza should benefit from head coach Klint Kubiak's sharp play-calling and talented pieces including center Tyler Linderbaum and tight end Brock Bowers. The Raiders' defense keeping Maxx Crosby at the deadline also should lower the threshold the offense needs to hit to win games. A blueprint Mendoza and the Raiders can hope for: Drake Maye's rookie season with the New England Patriots. Maye entered midseason with a struggling team (and particularly, a struggling offensive line) that won few games but created the foundation for him and the team to thrive in Year 2.

The Chargers' sense of reality: The 1-7 Titans, 2-7 Eagles and 2-7 Colts all gathered draft capital in recent days and weeks to bolster their future given this season's playoff hopes are lost. Why didn't the 0-8 Chargers, the league's only winless team for three weeks now, follow suit? Give the Chargers a morsel of credit for dealing linebacker Daiyan Henley just before the deadline. The Chargers sent their contract-year linebacker to the in-division Broncos in exchange for a 2027 fourth- and 2028 fifth-round pick, a person with knowledge of the deal confirmed to Yahoo Sports. But otherwise, there were head-scratching decisions. Why not offload veteran Khalil Mack's salary? Did the Chargers listen to offers on talented young edge Tuli Tuipulotu, even if his future value might not be worth shopping away? How about interior defensive lineman Dalvin Tomlinson as teams go all-in on defensive tackles? Much is wrong in Los Angeles right now, and the club has seemed unwilling to make changes at the staff or roster levels to fix it. The Chargers' trade-deadline passivity is just the latest reason to question Jim Harbaugh's grand plan.

articles.title: Dolphins add QB Malik Willis to IR due to lingering groin injury; Kyle McCord expected to start vs. Colts
articles.summary: Willis' injury is not considered season-ending.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins announced Tuesday that they are placing quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve .

Willis has had a lingering groin injury that has been impacting his mobility. The quarterback had an MRI, and it showed that it is now a core muscle injury. Willis doesn't need surgery, but the amount of rest required to recover necessitated an IR stint.

With Willis sidelined for at least the next month, backup quarterback Kyle McCord is expected to take over as the starter this weekend against the Indianapolis Colts, per ESPN's Adam Schefter . Willis is not expected to miss the remainder of the season.

Willis joined the Dolphins this offseason, signing a 3-year, $67.5 million deal in free agency. He reunited with new Miami head coach Jeff Hafley, who was with Willis last year in Green Bay as the defensive coordinator.

Willis has played in eight games this season and has thrown for 1,396 yards, 6 touchdowns and 6 interceptions.

The 27-year-old is known for being able to use his legs and has picked up 232 yards and three additional scores on the ground. Willis is currently Miami's second-leading rusher behind Ollie Gordon (463 yards, 4 TDs).

McCord was a sixth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft by the Philadelphia Eagles. He spent the season on Philadelphia's practice squad, but joined the Packers in the offseason on a reserve/futures contract.

The quarterback was then traded to the Dolphins in late August for a 2028 sixth-round pick to replace Quinn Ewers, whom Miami traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

McCord has yet to play a snap in his pro career, but that is expected to change Sunday against the Colts, as he is in line to make his first career start.

Brady Cook is currently Miami's only other quarterback, and he is on the practice squad.

articles.title: Cowboys Reportedly Sign New RB After 2026 NFL Trade Deadline, Tyler Goodson Injury
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys fans may have been hoping for a more consequential move ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET NFL trade deadline, but they reportedly did make a running back addition.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys fans may have been hoping for a more consequential move ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET NFL trade deadline, but they reportedly did make a running back addition.

Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News reported the Cowboys signed Kendre Miller to its practice squad with Tyler Goodson dealing with a knee injury he suffered in Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday that Goodson will miss "multiple weeks" with the setback.

The timing was less than ideal for Goodson, as he was just starting to establish himself in the running back rotation behind Javonte Williams.

He finished with a season-high 12 carries for 77 yards in the win over the Colts, which marked his second time in a three-game span with double-digit carries. Yet his injury put the team in scramble mode as it attempted to find another backup for Williams.

Enter Miller, whom ESPN's Todd Archer reported visited with the Cowboys on Tuesday before their decision to sign him.

The TCU product was available because the New Orleans Saints released him after he appeared in six games for the NFC South team this season. He ran for 159 yards and two touchdowns on an ugly 2.8 yards per carry in those six games.

Miller was also an occasional threat in the Saints' passing game with nine catches on a career-high 13 targets this season.

While he isn't someone who is going to carry the offense on his back, the Cowboys won't ask him to do so. Instead, he will surely be put in a role where he is expected to fill in for Williams on a handful of series throughout games to keep the starter fresher for the stretch run.

Next up for Dallas is a home game against the San Francisco 49ers.

articles.body:
NFL trade action has been going on for a few weeks now and finally culminated Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET.

Here's a look at the 17 in-season trades as well as big names that didn't get moved, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Here's a look at how social media reacted to all some action that went down on Tuesday morning and afternoon.

The Minnesota Vikings will reunite with quarterback Kirk Cousins, who played six seasons (2018-2023) with the team, after acquiring him from the Las Vegas Raiders for a third-round draft pick.

This was a much-needed pickup for the 6-2 Vikings, especially with Kyler Murray out with a Grade 2 hamstring strain and backup Carson Wentz struggling mightily (8-of-25, 85 yards, two interceptions) Monday in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

However, this looks good for the Raiders as well. Cousins was brought in as a bridge quarterback to give rookie Fernando Mendoza time before he took the reins. He performed the role well, and the Raiders got a draft pick out of it.

Cousins' first start will be Sunday at the Green Bay Packers. Mendoza is in line to make his first start on Sunday vs. the Seattle Seahawks.

The Indianapolis Colts did not trade running back Jonathan Taylor, who was long the subject of trade rumors this season. In the end, the Colts never got the package they wanted, per Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix.

The 2-7 Colts held a fire sale this year, dealing left guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs. However, Taylor is staying put.

It's a tough blow for teams hoping to land a three-time Pro Bowler and first team All-Pro. It's also a big risk for the Colts and perhaps a puzzling move overall.

Taylor, who is under contract through the 2028 season on a two-year, $44 million extension , has amassed 876 yards from scrimmage and eight touchdowns.

The Colts dealt wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a sixth-round draft pick and wideout Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs for fourth- and fifth-rounders. Indianapolis also sent Kansas City a seventh-rounder.

Allen, a 14-year veteran on a one-year contract, was an obvious choice to leave town with the team at 2-7. It's also a great move for the 7-1 49ers, who have been hit hard with injuries at wideout and need more help.

The six-time Pro Bowler has 40 catches for 351 yards and a touchdown.

As for Downs, this post should tell you how he feels about the trade (although he's also thankful for his time in town).

Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes had an eye on Downs' post.

This could be a good move for the 6-2 Chiefs, which needed pass-catching help. No wideout on the team has more than 300 receiving yards or two receiving touchdowns.

However, it's fair to say Downs, who is in the final season of a rookie contract, has been a bit disappointing this year. He hasn't eclipsed 50 or more receiving yards in his last six games or 25 or more yards in any of his last three.

Still, a change of scenery can do wonders for Downs, who had 140 catches over his first two seasons (2023-2024).

Downs has 33 catches foe 354 yards and a score in 2026.

Bengals Back Out of Arnold Ebiketie Trade With Eagles

The Cincinnati Bengals had a deal in place to add defensive end Arnold Ebiketie from the Philadelphia Eagles for a sixth-round pick, but the deal fell through.

Earlier in the day, Over The Cap contributor Nick Korte correctly pointed out that the Bengals would have lost a third-round compensatory pick after Trey Hendrickson left in free agency for the Baltimore Ravens.

Korte came through in the clutch a few years ago as well, per ESPN's Field Yates.

It's an odd situation, to say the least.

Ebiketie is in his fifth NFL season and first with the Eagles after four years with the Atlanta Falcons. He has 25 tackles in nine games.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Re-Signs With Vikings on Practice-Squad Contract, WR Released After Cousins Trade
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings released veteran wideout Odell Beckham Jr. on Tuesday, per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo, after he was elevated from the practice squad to the team's active roster ahead of Monday night's 23-6 loss vs. the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings released veteran wideout Odell Beckham Jr. on Tuesday, per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , after he was elevated from the practice squad to the team's active roster ahead of Monday night's 23-6 loss vs. the Buffalo Bills.

His time in Minnesota isn't over, however. The Vikings reportedly are re-signing him to the practice squad, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . His release was likely a mechanism to clear a roster spot for the recently-acquired Kirk Cousins.

He didn't record any receptions during Monday's game and played just two snaps .

Beckham, 34, started the 2026 season with the New York Giants, a reunion with the team that originally drafted him and where he played his best football. But the second time around wasn't terribly memorable—he played just 19 snaps across three games and didn't register a catch before being released on Sept. 29.

He then signed with the Vikings to the practice squad on Oct. 7.

Beckham was once one of the NFL's ascending superstars, earning Pro Bowl honors in each of his first three seasons after recording at least 90 catches, 1,300 receiving yards and double-digit touchdowns in those campaigns.

But major injury issues and a falling out with both the Giants and later the Cleveland Browns followed. Since 2022, Beckham has appeared in just 27 total games and at this point seems like little more than emergency depth for the Vikings.

Kirk Cousins reacted to getting traded from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

Cousins thanked Raiders fans for their support while telling former teammate Fernando Mendoza to "go get em" in a post on his Instagram story.

Expectations are high for Mendoza, as he joined Las Vegas following a 2025 campaign at Indiana in which he earned Heisman Trophy honors and led the Hoosiers to a national championship.

articles.title: The top 5 biggest impact deadline trades, including Jaguars and Bears shooting for a Super Bowl
articles.summary: Two defensive tackles are included in the most impactful in-season trades this year.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline had plenty of action.

There were multiple teams who traded for a new starting quarterback. Stars at all three levels of the defense were dealt. There were well-known offensive linemen and receivers moved. Strangely, after weeks of chatter, the only position that didn't see a trade was running back. But there were enough deals to keep everyone busy.

Here are the five most impactful trades made since the start of this season:

Simmons showed in his first game at Seattle how much he will impact the Bears this season. Chicago's defense looked much different with Simmons in the middle, taking up attention from blockers and still making plays. He was a first-team All-Pro last season and could be on a similar path this season. Everyone saw Simmons' dominance, yet the Bears were the team that acted on it. Chicago sent two first-round draft picks to Tennessee for Simmons , who is 29 years old, but the Bears and their fans won't mind if he helps break a Super Bowl drought that dates back to the 1985 season. Given how good Chicago's offense is and how the defense has improved already with Simmons in the middle, it's realistic to think Chicago could find itself in the Super Bowl.

"I think he's just — I don't know — you can feel his presence," linebacker T.J. Edwards said after Simmons' Week 8 Bears debut, according to the team's site . "Especially me, I'm right behind him, so I can kind of just feel how they're trying to block him. … They made our job a whole lot easier. But he definitely helps, for sure."

The Eagles had a lot of potential trade chips, but Davis wasn't discussed as one because he was just 26 years old and also one of the highest-paid defensive tackles in the NFL. But the Jaguars got aggressive, sending a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for a player who immediately can replace (and potentially upgrade) from DaVon Hamilton, who was having a tremendous season before he tore his quadriceps and went to injured reserve. It was a very expensive trade, and probably an overpay, but Davis unquestionably makes the Jaguars stronger this season.

The Jaguars also made moves for safety Jessie Bates III and another defensive tackle, Davon Godchaux, but the move for Davis is the big difference-maker for a team that has Super Bowl hopes.

We have to be careful to not overrate the impact of this move. The Vikings still have the fourth-best quarterback and fourth-best offense in their division. Cousins is 38 years old. And many of the same people who were clamoring for the Vikings to trade for Cousins were the same ones who, during Cousins' previous six seasons in Minnesota, said he could never win anything.

This is a rare move in the NFL as viable starting quarterbacks are hardly available in a trade. The Vikings didn't pay too much, a third-round pick , and it's the unique situation of a quarterback who has played with the coach and in the scheme before. He can step right in. The Vikings have a fantastic defense and now should have a competent offense. Wherever this reunion leads, it was smart for the Vikings to find out.

Hooker is having a career year in his eighth season. He leads the NFL with five interceptions. His Pro Football Focus grade ranks fourth among safeties with at least 300 snaps. The Bills had a hole at the position after cutting C. J. Gardner-Johnson and did well to land Hooker.

The Bills' defense started slow this season and while it has played well for two weeks, that came against quarterbacks Joe Fagnano and Carson Wentz. Buffalo needed a defensive upgrade. The Bills are pretty good up front, and now they have a potential All-Pro safety this season for the back end. It was a sharp move that should improve the Bills , who are in a great spot to make the Super Bowl for the first time in the Josh Allen era.

When the Giants traded a fifth-round pick for McCarthy, it seemed like a low-cost gamble on a reclamation project . The Giants couldn't have known they had found a starting quarterback for a team that is first in the NFC East. McCarthy had a blistering fourth quarter in relief of Jameis Winston against the Saints, throwing for 243 yards in less than a quarter. He got the starting job after that and the Giants have won both games since.

It's possible McCarthy reverts to the inconsistent form he had last season, which caused the Vikings to give up on the 10th overall pick of the 2024 NFL Draft after only 10 starts. But he has looked poised and gives the Giants a more stable option at quarterback than the hot-and-cold Winston. It seemed like the Giants' season might have been done when Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury in Week 2, but a smart and cheap trade for McCarthy could end up saving it.

articles.title: "It meant the world": Travis Kelce's $30,000 gesture changes 79-year-old woman's life after 56 years in her home
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has spent years making headlines for his achievements with the Kansas City Chiefs, but one of his most meaningful contributions came far away
articles.body: Travis Kelce has spent years making headlines for his achievements with the Kansas City Chiefs, but one of his most meaningful contributions came far away from the football field. The NFL star stepped forward when 79-year-old Gloria White faced the possibility of losing the comfort of her longtime home. Through his Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation, Kelce provided a $30,000 grant that helped fund major repairs to her house. The contribution did more than fix a damaged property. It gave a longtime Kansas City resident a chance to continue living in the place filled with decades of memories.Travis Kelce's $30,000 donation helps Gloria White stay in her homeGloria White had spent 56 years in her eastern Kansas City home, raising her family and welcoming children from the neighbourhood into her backyard. However, age and health challenges had made everyday life increasingly difficult. She suffered from arthritis and joint pain, which affected her mobility and made several parts of the house unsafe.The problems were not limited to minor maintenance. Sewage had leaked into her basement, the steps leading downstairs were broken, and the property needed significant plumbing work. Her roof, gutters, bathroom and kitchen also required attention.White initially contacted Rebuilding Together Kansas City, a nonprofit organisation that helps vulnerable residents live safely in their homes. The organisation then partnered with Kelce's foundation to make the necessary improvements possible.According to Rebuilding Together Kansas City, Eighty-Seven & Running provided a $30,000 grant towards the project. The repairs were completed in early December 2023, covering everything from plumbing problems to important safety modifications.The project included a new roof, bathroom and kitchen improvements, grab bars, additional railings and repairs to the home's major plumbing systems. These changes helped White move around more comfortably and reduced the risks she faced inside her house.Gloria White shares emotional reaction to Travis Kelce's gestureRebuilding Together Kansas City executive director Scott Hickox appreciated Kelce's involvement and explained how much the partnership meant to the community.“For Travis to care enough and his foundation to care enough about his community and what’s happening in our city, it meant the world”.For White, the improvements meant something far more personal than a renovated kitchen or repaired roof. They allowed her to hold on to the home where she had spent most of her adult life.She also expressed her gratitude for the unexpected support, saying, “I thank God so much for the work they did here at my house,” she said. “You never know which way your blessing will come, but it will be at the right time.”White's story also reflects the community spirit she had built over the years. She had regularly welcomed neighbourhood children into her backyard and encouraged them to follow their ambitions.“I've had all races of kids in my backyard. I've taught them; don’t ever think you can’t wait; keep on and you pursue it," White said.For Kelce, the $30,000 contribution through his foundation became an opportunity to support someone who had spent decades giving back to her neighbourhood. His gesture helped ensure that White could continue making memories in the home she never wanted to leave.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Colts had Jonathan Taylor and Grover Stewart trade offers but didn't complete deals that eventually got pulled
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts turned down multiple Jonathan Taylor trade offers, including a second-round pick from the New York Giants, holding out for more.
articles.body: The NFL trade deadline came and went Tuesday afternoon and the Indianapolis Colts underperformed – kind of like they've been doing on the field this season. The Colts were offered multiple trades for running back Jonathan Taylor in the last week, league sources told OutKick and Fox News Digital, adding that several of those offers included multiple picks and even high draft picks. But the Colts were intent on getting some sort of blockbuster deal for Taylor. And they did not get that, so they did not trade Taylor. The Colts also engaged in conversations with at least one other team (the Minnesota Vikings, one source said) about Daniel Jones but kept their embattled starting quarterback. MORE PROOF THAT ANY TEAM TRADING FOR DANIEL JONES AT THE NFL TRADE DEADLINE IS CHASING FOOL'S GOLD The Colts did, however, trade a pair of solid but not outstanding receivers in Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Excuse us while we yawn. COLTS GM CHRIS BALLARD ON KEENAN ALLEN DUI ARREST: 'HE'S A TREMENDOUS HUMAN BEING. GIVE HIM SOME GRACE' The Colts added a fourth- and fifth-round pick for Downs in their trade with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Colts also added a sixth-round pick in 2027 from the San Francisco 49ers for Allen. Both Downs and Allen moving on make sense in that Downs asked to be traded a couple of weeks ago, Allen is 34 years old, and both are playing on expiring contracts. COLTS TRADE PRO BOWL GUARD QUENTON NELSON TO SEAHAWKS, THE FIRST OF WHAT COULD BE MULTIPLE DEADLINE MOVES But it's the stuff the Colts failed to do that raises eyebrows. They had a trade for Taylor in the offing the last week or so. Fox Sports reported that offer was from the New York Giants and would have brought a second-round and fifth-round pick for Taylor. JONATHAN TAYLOR DELIVERS WHAT SOUNDS LIKE A GOODBYE TO INDIANAPOLIS AFTER COLTS' FIFTH STRAIGHT LOSS And they decided not to pull the trigger. That trade would have sent the Colts a package somewhat similar to one the San Francisco 49ers gave up for Christian McCaffrey, but as the Colts considered the offer, the Giants pulled it. The Colts wanted a deal that included more picks or a higher pick than the No. 2 selection. Yes, the Colts wanted a No. 1 pick for Taylor. And no one offered that, so the club informed Taylor he wasn't being traded. The same with Jones as he seemed to know by early Tuesday afternoon that he was not going to be traded. The Colts had other opportunities to make trades to increase their future draft capital but apparently dithered. A league source told OutKick and Fox News Digital that the Colts could have traded starting defensive tackle Grover Stewart for a fifth-round pick. The offer was upgraded to a fourth-round pick and another late-round pick. But as the Colts waited to get an even better offer, all offers were pulled. So Stewart remains with the team. The messaging the Colts apparently put out through various media outlets after Tuesday's trade deadline anticlimax surrounding Taylor is simply astounding: They didn't want have a garage sale that could potentially hurt their ability to hire a top general manager or perhaps head coach if current coach Shane Steichen is fired after this season. They kept Taylor and Jones to use them as a lure for a future executive or coach. That, by the way, is ridiculous reasoning. The Colts wanted to keep two players that haven't been able to lift the current team above its 2-7 record as a way of somehow convincing a future unidentified GM or head coach to work in Indy. That is illogical because a future GM or coach might want the use of more draft picks to build their team in whatever image they wish rather than inheriting players currently on the team. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! And this: It is quite possible that after spending the last couple of weeks on trade watch, and delivering what sounded like a farewell message following Sunday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys, Taylor might be disappointed he's still on a losing team instead of headed to a team that wanted him for a postseason push. The Colts have been a grand disappointment this season. And their work leading right up to the NFL trade deadline was more of the same. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy was in front of the cameras when he learned that his former team, the Minnesota Vikings, traded for Kirk Cousins on Tuesday.

"Wish him nothing but the best of luck," he told reporters when informed of the trade during a press conference. "I know he's loved in that building so it'll be a great fit."

The Vikings have had plenty of quarterback turnover in the past year, signing Kyler Murray in the offseason before trading McCarthy—a former first-round pick—to the New York Giants in late September for a 2027 fifth-round pick. Cousins was acquired on Tuesday from the Las Vegas Raiders for a third-round selection.

McCarthy, 23, has since supplanted Jameis Winston as the starting quarterback with Jaxson Dart out for at least the remainder of the regular season. In four total appearances and two starts, McCarthy has thrown for 622 yards, a touchdown and an interception while rushing for 51 yards. The Giants are 2-0 in his starts.

Thus far, the Giants have felt like a far better fit for McCarthy than the Vikings. In Minnesota, the hope is that Cousins can finally solve what has been a major quarterback issue.

articles.title: NFL trade deadline winners and losers, including Dianna Russini and Kirk Cousins
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins gives the Minnesota Vikings a major QB upgrade as the Los Angeles Chargers bizarrely held on to veterans with expiring contracts.
articles.body: Here are the winners and losers of the 2026 NFL trade deadline: Winner: Minnesota Vikings While a 38-year-old Kirk Cousins is hardly glamorous, he's considerably better than Carson Wentz, Kyler Murray or any other realistic option the Vikings had. He's also still an above-average quarterback, currently second in the NFL in passing touchdowns. With an elite defense already in place, Cousins immediately improves Minnesota's chances of holding on to the lead in the historically competitive NFC North. BOBBY BURACK: DIANNA RUSSINI WANTS SYMPATHY WITHOUT ACCOUNTABILITY IN MIKE VRABEL SCANDAL Loser: Los Angeles Chargers The Chargers appear determined to become the first team to start 0-8 and make the playoffs. Either that, or they're the biggest losers of the entire deadline. The reports were true. The Chargers held on to veterans with expiring contracts, including Khalil Mack and Donte Jackson, both of whom could have fetched solid draft capital in return. The team did, however, trade its homegrown, emerging linebacker Daiyan Henley – to the division rival Denver Broncos. Winner: Chicago Bears The Bears were quiet on deadline day because they made their move two weeks ago. No team improved more through a trade this season than Chicago did by acquiring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Simmons has made an immediate impact in Chicago, improving the play of the defenders around him, notably Devin Bush and Austin Booker. Most sportsbooks have moved the Bears from 10th to third in Super Bowl odds in recent weeks. Trading for Simmons is part of the reason. Loser: Jacksonville Jaguars The Jaguars improved by trading for safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis. But they vastly overpaid for both, to the point of recklessness. Jacksonville sent the Eagles a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for Davis. He is a good player, but primarily a run-stuffing nose tackle. The Jaguars paid as if he were a difference-making pass rusher. He isn't. They also sent Atlanta a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick for Bates. The problem: Bates is a free agent after the season, and the Jaguars are projected to be over the salary cap. What's more, the Bills acquired fellow safety Amani Hooker at a much better price. articles.title: Tom Brady's plea for dying mentor sparked 600 donor registrations before unexpected kidney donation saved mother of two
articles.summary: In 2012, Tom Brady wanted to save the life of a man who had shaped his football career.
articles.body: In 2012, Tom Brady wanted to save the life of a man who had shaped his football career. But his emotional appeal for a kidney donor ended up changing another family's future in an unexpected way. The New England Patriots legend reached out to the public when his longtime mentor, Tom Martinez, desperately needed a transplant. Around 600 people responded to the appeal. Martinez never received the kidney he needed, but one man's decision to donate eventually gave a mother of two a second chance at life. It became one of the most remarkable stories connected to Brady's life away from football.Tom Brady's emotional kidney donor appeal brings 600 responsesMartinez was more than a football coach to Tom Brady. He had worked with the quarterback since his teenage years and played an important role in developing his throwing technique. Their relationship continued long after Brady entered the NFL.However, Martinez faced a serious health crisis when his kidneys began failing. He needed a transplant, and finding a suitable donor became increasingly urgent.Brady decided to use his public profile to help. He appealed to people to register as potential kidney donors through MatchingDonors.com, hoping someone could help the man who had guided him throughout his career.The response was remarkable. Around 600 people registered after Brady's appeal attracted widespread attention.Sadly, Martinez died in February 2012 before receiving a transplant. His death was a devastating loss for Brady, who had hoped to repay his mentor in some way.Yet the appeal had already set something unexpected in motion.Peter Hughes donates kidney to save mother of two Ajisa BethielAmong the people who responded to Brady's appeal was Peter Hughes, a resident of Sterling, Massachusetts. Although Martinez could not receive his donation, Hughes decided that he still wanted to help someone in need.His decision eventually brought him to Ajisa Bethiel, a mother of two from Lexington, Massachusetts.Bethiel had escaped war-torn Bosnia in 1994 and later faced serious kidney problems. Finding a suitable donor was difficult, and her future remained uncertain while she waited for a transplant.Hughes eventually donated one of his kidneys to Bethiel at Massachusetts General Hospital in May 2012.The transplant gave Bethiel a new opportunity to live a healthier life and spend more time with her children.Brady's original intention had been to help his beloved coach. Although that effort could not save Martinez, the public appeal encouraged hundreds of people to consider organ donation. One man's decision ultimately helped save another person's life.It was an extraordinary reminder that a single act of kindness can reach far beyond its original purpose. Brady never set out to change Bethiel's life, but his determination to help his mentor helped create an opportunity that she desperately needed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Buffalo Bills running back James Cook reacted to speculation that he had an accident during the team's 23-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night.

"This is wild I didn't s--t on myself," Cook wrote alongside several crying laughing emojis in a Tuesday post on X.

The three-time Pro Bowler finished with 107 yards and a touchdown on 31 carries during the lopsided victory.

Cook has remained a key piece of Buffalo's offense this season, ranking No. 5 among all players with 814 rush yards while averaging 4.8 yards per carry. He's also found the end zone eight times.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo Reacts to Giants Not Trading for RB After Jonathan Taylor Rumors at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo remained confident in himself after the New York Giants chose not to add another running back before Tuesday's trade deadline.
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo remained confident in himself after the New York Giants chose not to add another running back before Tuesday's trade deadline.

"You've seen what I can do," Skattebo said Tuesday, per Darryl Slater of NJ.com (h/t Josh Alper of Pro Football Talk). "When I come out and I'm ready to play football, I can be one of the most dangerous backs in the league. Simple as that."

On Friday, Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer reported that the Giants were a "serious suitor" for Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor.

Two days later, Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported that New York offered a second-round pick and a fifth-round selection for Taylor before pulling the offer.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh discussed the reported negotiations on Sunday.

"I'm not saying that report's not true. Those conversations are taking place," Harbaugh said, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan . "If something happens for any player, can't talk about any [specific] player because they're with other teams right now, but we're not ruling anything out."

Discussions between New York and Indianapolis appeared to break down, as Raanan reported Monday that "it would be a surprise at this point if Jonathan Taylor is traded to the Giants."

Skattebo has appeared in seven games during his second year in New York, although he missed the team's Week 9 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles due to a hamstring injury .

The 24-year-old has rushed for 418 yards and two touchdowns this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry. He's also caught 11 passes for 76 yards.

The Giants currently sit atop the NFC East standings with a 5-2-1 record as they look to end a three-year playoff drought.

The in-season loss of Jalen Hurts has precipitated some of this movement, but the Eagles were already in sell mode with the Cam Jurgens trade the week prior to Hurts being diagnosed with blood clots. articles.title: "I have no power in my left leg": Tyreek Hill's NFL return hits a wall as latest injury update complicates Chiefs reunion

articles.body: Tyreek Hill's hopes of returning to the NFL have hit another roadblock, and the latest development could make a reunion with the Kansas City Chiefs even harder to achieve. The explosive wide receiver has spent more than a year trying to recover from a devastating knee injury. Yet, despite months of rehabilitation and optimism from his agent, questions remain about his readiness to play. With the season moving forward and Kansas City looking for offensive help, Hill's health could decide whether one of the NFL's most talked-about potential reunions has any chance of happening.Tyreek Hill injury update raises concerns over NFL comebackTyreek Hill has not played since September 29, 2025, when he suffered a serious left knee injury during the Miami Dolphins' game against the New York Jets. The injury involved a dislocated knee and a torn ACL, followed by surgery and a long recovery.Now 32, the eight-time Pro Bowl receiver is still working to regain the strength and speed that made him such a dangerous threat. Kansas City reporter Pete Sweeney recently offered a concerning update during a conversation with Trey Wingo. He indicated that Hill might not yet be ready to pass the medical examination required before signing with an NFL team."We had kind of heard locally that Tyreek Hill wouldn't really be ready to pass a physical, take the field until early to mid November," Sweeney said.That projected window has now arrived, but Hill remains without a contract. It does not mean his comeback is over. However, teams will need proof that his knee can handle the demands of an NFL season before making a commitment.Hill also described the physical challenge in a rehabilitation video shared in July."So it's about 10 months after doing two surgeries," Hill explained in a rehabilitation video. "My left leg is the one that I injured. I have no power in my left leg at all, so I'm trying to regain all the power back in my left leg. But it's one day at a time."Patrick Mahomes reunion faces fresh questions as Chiefs weigh optionsA return to Kansas City would carry plenty of emotion. Hill spent six seasons with the Chiefs after they drafted him in 2016. He recorded 479 catches for 6,630 yards and 56 touchdowns before joining Miami in 2022. He also helped the franchise win Super Bowl LIV alongside Patrick Mahomes.But a familiar connection may not be enough to secure a deal. Sweeney also pointed to questions about Hill's off-field history and whether the Chiefs would want him back in their locker room."It's the type of player as well that it's 'do we want to bring this player into the locker room?' Just considering some of the off-the-field stuff, but at a certain point, the Chiefs showed us two weeks ago the off-the-field to them maybe doesn't matter."Those concerns include an October 2026 civil jury verdict that found Hill liable on two battery claims involving his estranged wife. The jury awarded $500,000 in compensatory damages. This was a civil finding, not a criminal conviction.Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has remained hopeful about his recovery and said in October that the receiver was close to full fitness. Talks with several teams have also reportedly taken place.Still, there is no confirmed contract or return date. Until Hill passes a physical, his NFL future and any possible reunion with Mahomes remain uncertain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New Steelers Rumors Reveal WRs Targeted in 'Aggressive' Pursuit Before NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers poked around the trade market for wide receivers but ultimately didn't pull the trigger ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, per Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette:
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers poked around the trade market for wide receivers but ultimately didn't pull the trigger ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, per Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette :

According to Chris Halicke of DK Pittsburgh Sports, the Steelers had talks with the Jacksonville Jaguars regarding Brian Thomas Jr. and the Tennessee Titans for Calvin Ridley.

Per that report, "The Steelers were most aggressive in pursuing Thomas and believed a deal was possible, but the Jaguars wound up deciding to not trade him at all. The Jaguars did not want to trade Thomas to another AFC opponent, especially one that's on the schedule in a few weeks. The Steelers also pursued Ridley, but his altercation with a valet driver at Nashville International Airport over the weekend impacted those negotiations, as well."

The Steelers also reportedly "checked in" on Josh Downs but "did not aggressively pursue a trade" before the Indianapolis Colts dealt him to the Kansas City Chiefs.

Remaining stagnant on Tuesday will likely irk quarterback Aaron Rodgers. The Steelers have been pretty ho-hum in the passing game this season, ranking 19th in yardage (210.5 YPG) and tied for 15th in passing scores (13).

And the connection between Rodgers and DK Metcalf hasn't meaningfully evolved across two seasons. Last year, Metcalf caught 59 passes for 850 yards and six touchdowns. This season he's pulled in 33 catches for 378 yards and a score, a 17-game pace of 70 catches for 803 yards and two touchdowns.

Rookie Germie Bernard has flashed at times and Rodgers has plenty of underneath options in tight ends Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth. But the Steelers aren't scaring too many defenses over the top.

What they are doing well is running the football and playing defense. Jaylen Warren (704 yards, two touchdowns on the ground; 25 catches for 294 yards and another score in the passing game), while the defense is giving up just 18 points per game (tied for fourth in the NFL).

But it's fair to wonder if a lack of dynamic playmakers at receiver will ultimately cap their upside.

Of course, there's no guarantee that either Thomas or Ridley would have been true game-changers in Pittsburgh. The former has continued to be an absolute afterthought in Jacksonville, following up a disappointing 2025 season with just 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns this year. Perhaps a change of scenery is needed, but Thomas hasn't put out great tape for two seasons now.

Meanwhile, Ridley has appeared in just 14 games over the past two seasons and only managed 23 catches for 394 yards during that time. The 31-year-old's best football appears to be behind him.

articles.title: Raiders GM Explains Kirk Cousins Trade, Praises Fernando Mendoza After Surprise Vikings Deal
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders did not tell Kirk Cousins they were going to move him before they traded the quarterback to the Minnesota Vikings for a third-round draft pick because they did not expect there was going to be a trade on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders did not tell Kirk Cousins they were going to move him before they traded the quarterback to the Minnesota Vikings for a third-round draft pick because they did not expect there was going to be a trade on Tuesday.

"There was nothing to speak about," general manager John Spytek told reporters when revealing he didn't speak to Cousins before the move. "We didn't have any expectation that this was coming."

Spytek also said Las Vegas wasn't actively shopping him and "never made one call on Kirk Cousins. I got a few phone calls, but one real one this morning."

That the Raiders traded Cousins comes as no surprise.

While they are still in the AFC playoff picture at 4-5, they also selected Fernando Mendoza with the No. 1 overall pick of the 2026 NFL draft. They were eventually going to turn to him as the franchise quarterback of the future, and Cousins was largely just a placeholder until the Indiana product was ready.

Minnesota, which needed a quarterback to pair with its dominant defense, also offered a solid draft pick and familiar landing spot for the veteran.

"We (were) all staring the future in the face here with Fernando, and Kirk was very open with that when we got him," Spytek said . "We had to decide: Do we want to go forward here over the last eight games, or do we want to take what Minnesota is offering right now? Ultimately, we decided to do that."

Spytek also believes the top draft pick is ready for the spotlight, adding Mendoza "passed every test."

He continued and said, "It's something that he's worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building. I want to stop short of saying he's earned it, but he put us in a position where we had to make a really hard decision today, with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback."

As for Cousins, he played for the Vikings from 2018 through 2023 and was a three-time Pro Bowler during that span. He also threw for more than 4,000 yards in four different seasons and already has chemistry with No. 1 receiver Justin Jefferson.

It should be an easy transition for the signal-caller, who will now look to lead the Vikings to the Super Bowl following their 6-2 start.

From the Vikings' perspective, they likely had plenty of urgency when it came to the quarterback position this season. Kyler Murray is dealing with a hamstring injury, while Carson Wentz was terrible in his place during Monday's loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Wentz finished 8-of-25 for 81 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions as the offense struggled throughout the game. Murray hasn't exactly been great either with just five touchdown passes to three interceptions through six games.

Ideally for the Vikings, Cousins will come in and elevate the ceiling for a team that is already in the middle of the NFC playoff race.

articles.body: Six Flags, the amusement park giant associated with Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce, has agreed to an $11.2 million settlement following allegations that customers faced hidden fees while booking tickets online. The case could bring cash payments to more than 1.4 million eligible California customers. Although the lawsuit does not involve Kelce personally, his reported connection to the company adds a celebrity angle to a dispute over ticket prices and consumer rights.The settlement also raises a familiar question for families planning a day out: How much should a ticket really cost? For some customers, the answer allegedly changed just before they paid.Six Flags faces $11.2 million settlement over hidden ticket feesThe legal dispute began in June 2024 when Sargis Isayan filed a class-action lawsuit against Cedar Fair, L.P., which operated Knott's Berry Farm and California's Great America.According to court documents cited by PEOPLE, Isayan accused the operator of the “unlawful practice of ‘drip pricing.’ ”The complaint alleged that customers saw one ticket price while browsing, only to encounter an extra processing charge during checkout.Isayan argued that the added fee offered no real benefit. By the time customers reached the payment page, many had already spent time choosing tickets and were less likely to cancel their purchase.Cedar Fair merged with Six Flags Entertainment Corporation in July 2024, bringing the parks under the combined business.Six Flags has not admitted wrongdoing. Instead, the company agreed to resolve the dispute through an $11.2 million settlement, subject to court approval.The case highlights a wider concern about online pricing. When businesses reveal extra charges late in a transaction, customers may struggle to compare the true cost of different options.Travis Kelce-linked Six Flags settlement: Who qualifies for the $8 payout?The settlement comes as Travis Kelce's reported ambassador and investor ties to Six Flags draw attention to the amusement park business. However, there is no indication that the Chiefs tight end participated in the alleged pricing practices or played any role in the lawsuit.The proposed agreement covers California customers who bought eligible non-season tickets online for Knott's Berry Farm, Knott's Soak City or California's Great America between June 28, 2020, and July 1, 2024.Customers must also have entered a California billing ZIP code and paid a processing fee.Approximately 1,405,235 people may qualify.Eligible customers who submit valid claims can receive $8 in cash. Those who do not file will automatically receive an $8 voucher for future purchases through Six Flags, provided they qualify under the settlement terms.The vouchers expire 36 months after issuance.Customers seeking cash must submit their claims by December 22, 2026, through the official settlement website, final approval hearing is scheduled for March 30, 2027. articles.title: Raiders rookie QB Fernando Mendoza will make first career start vs. Seahawks after Kirk Cousins trade: 'He's prepared'
articles.summary: Mendoza, this year's No. 1 overall pick, had the opportunity to learn under Cousins before and during the season.
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza, a reigning college national champion, will face the defending Super Bowl champions in his first career NFL start.

Mendoza, who led Indiana on a storybook run to College Football Playoff glory, will get the nod for the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium against the Seattle Seahawks, general manager John Spytek and head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed Tuesday .

Mendoza, the No. 1 overall draft pick in April, is up for a 4-5 Raiders team that traded veteran Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 third-round pick hours before Tuesday's trade deadline. That deal effectively marked the beginning of the Mendoza era in Vegas.

"This is something that he's worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building," said Spytek, who emphasized in a news conference alongside Kubiak that the Cousins trade doesn't mean the Raiders are punting on the season or looking ahead to 2027.

Spytek added, regarding Mendoza: "He passed every test. I want to stop short of saying he's earned it, but he put us in a position where we had to make a really hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback."

After learning under the 38-year-old Cousins before and during the season, the 23-year-old Mendoza is set for quite the three-game test in advance of the Raiders' Week 13 bye.

Not only will he have to battle the Seahawks' vaunted defense, but he'll have to go up against the Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns the subsequent two weeks. Entering Week 10, all three of those teams rank inside the top 13 in fewest points per game allowed this season. The Broncos and Browns are tied with a handful of teams for fourth in the NFL with 26 sacks.

Mendoza has attempted only eight regular-season passes. All of those came in relief of Cousins down the stretch of a 45-17 road loss to the New England Patriots . That was part of a four-game Raiders skid that followed their head-turning 3-0 start .

In his first year at the helm, Kubiak named Cousins the team's Week 1 starter after evaluating both him and Mendoza in the preseason. He then stuck with Cousins under center despite the October losing streak .

Cousins was open throughout his stay in Las Vegas that he was well aware of the circumstances of his role and that his time as Raiders QB1 was limited. He stressed that he wanted to put the team in the best position to win games, even if that meant at some point handing the baton to Mendoza.

But Cousins played so well that he kept his job leading up to the deadline. In fact, an ESPN report surfaced Sunday morning, detailing how, at the time, the Raiders weren't interested in dealing him .

Spytek, Kubiak met with Cousins before making trade

Spytek explained Tuesday that the trade really came together with the Vikings that morning.

"I never made one call on Kirk Cousins," Spytek said, when asked if the Raiders were shopping Cousins. "I got a few phone calls, but one real one this morning."

Both Spytek and Kubiak were effusive about Cousins in the fallout of the trade. Spytek even divulged that, before Las Vegas made the final call on dealing Cousins, he and Kubiak sat with the longtime signal-caller to talk him through the deal.

"We both felt like it was important that he have say in it, too," Spytek said. "Fifteen-year veteran, everything he's given to this organization, he has a family and we kind of presented him with what we had on the table, and we tried to make the best decision. I think we owed him that respect."

Kubiak noted: "It reinforced how extremely unselfish he is and just the way that he spoke to us and the maturity and the awareness of the situation — I think we all left that room on the same page, all with respect for one another."

Cousins turned back the clock while working with Kubiak, posting a 20:8 touchdown-to-interception ratio. His 20 TD passes are good for second most in the league and already more than he's had in a season since his 2022 campaign with the Vikings, with whom he played from 2018-2023.

Cousins turned out to be among the best NFL rentals in recent memory. The Raiders paid him a total of $650,000, per ESPN's Field Yates , and his value resulted in a third-round pick and priceless mentorship.

He appeared to forge an endearing friendship with Mendoza, who eagerly absorbed tips and tricks from Cousins.

Kubiak said Tuesday that Cousins' influence "will remain on our team throughout this season."

He added: "And it remains with Fernando."

Kubiak clearly satisfied with patient approach to developing Mendoza

Kubiak was asked directly Tuesday if he feels like it helped Mendoza that he wasn't thrown in from Day 1.

"I do," Kubiak said with a soft smile. "Yes, I do. I think with the right role model, that will accelerate his growth, and we had the right role model."

Las Vegas drafted Mendoza first overall in the aftermath of his prolific 2025 season with the Hoosiers. He won the Heisman Trophy, vaulted himself into the end zone en route to beating Miami in the national title game and finished the season with 48 total touchdowns, including 41 through the air.

His effervescence, often on full display in postgame interviews, made him a unique college football star. He's still that happy-go-lucky QB , at least outside the white lines.

Time will tell how Mendoza's game translates to NFL regular-season play. He completed 6 of 8 passes against the Patriots for 48 yards. In the preseason, he had mixed results, impressing in his debut against the Arizona Cardinals and then throwing a pick-6 versus the Houston Texans and another interception against the San Francisco 49ers.

Mendoza wrapped the preseason with 240 yards on 25-of-45 passing, registering a 55.6% completion rate, one touchdown pass and those two picks.

It's been months since then, however. The Cousins trade speaks to Minnesota's desperation for a quarterback solution, but it also says a lot about the Raiders' trust in Mendoza's development.

"He's prepared, he's practiced extremely well," Kubiak said, "and his work habits also allow us to make this trade because we feel that he's ready to go, and we're excited to have him take the ball for the game here on Sunday."

Kubiak also said: "We knew this day was coming. We didn't know when it was going to be, but he's continued to grow since he's been here."
