articles.title: Reggie Wayne Jokes About Being Player-Coach After Colts Trade Josh Downs, Keenan Allen At Deadline
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts wide receivers coach and franchise legend Reggie Wayne joked on social media that he might have to return as a player-coach after the team traded wideouts Keenan Allen and Josh Downs on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receivers coach and franchise legend Reggie Wayne joked on social media that he might have to return as a player-coach after the team traded wideouts Keenan Allen and Josh Downs on Tuesday.

The fire sale-conducting Colts, who are 2-7, dealt Allen to the San Francisco 49ers for a sixth-round pick and Downs (plus a seventh-rounder) to the Kansas City Chiefs for fourth- and fifth-round selections before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline.

Indianapolis previously traded left guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. Running back Jonathan Taylor was long the subject of trade rumors and speculation but ultimately stayed in town.

Wayne starred on the Colts from 2001-2014. The six-time Pro Bowler and three-time All-Pro (one First Team, two Second Teams) amassed 1,070 catches for 14,345 yards and 82 touchdowns in his 14-year career. He had eight 1,000-yard seasons, including a career- and NFL-high 1,510 in 2007.

Wayne turns 48 years old on Nov. 17. Remarkably, he wouldn't be the oldest-ever player if he suited up this year. That honor goes to NFL legend George Blanda, who threw three passes for the Oakland Raiders at the age of 48 years, three months and four days on Dec. 21, 1975.

Perhaps Wayne can give the Colts a few more snaps in the final eight weeks of the season. If not, he has some work to do coaching up the remaining Colt wideouts on the active roster as they get pushed into heavier usage: Deion Burks, Ashton Dulin, Anthony Gould, Laquon Treadwell and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine. The Colts also have Alec Pierce, who unfortunately is on injured reserve with a re-injury of left heel/ankle issue.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor's Wife Reacts to Colts RB Not Being Traded at NFL Deadline in New TikTok Video
articles.summary: Jonathan Taylor's wife, Ayanna, reacted to the Indianapolis Colts choosing to keep the star running back beyond Tuesday's trade deadline.
articles.body:
Jonathan Taylor's wife, Ayanna, reacted to the Indianapolis Colts choosing to keep the star running back beyond Tuesday's trade deadline.

Ayanna posted a video of herself blowing kisses at the camera on TikTok along with the text, "Pov: you were stressed and delirious BUT it turned out you were worried for nothing!!"

"Not the last 2 weeks stressing us out & the NFL trade deadline is finally over!!" she wrote in the caption of the post. "Anyway, where were we?"

Ayanna previously called out the uncertainty surrounding her husband's future on the Colts leading up to the deadline in several social media posts .

ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Oct. 31 that the the Colts were "open" to parting ways with Taylor and were in "active and ongoing" trade discussions.

The three-time Pro Bowler was linked to the Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and Denver Broncos on the trade market.

Indianapolis ultimately decided to stick with Taylor, as he's set to close out his seventh season as a member of the team.

The Colts, who own a mere 2-7 record, still made several moves prior to the deadline.

They traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks before sending defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 27.

Indianapolis also dealt veteran wideout Keenan Allen to the 49ers on Tuesday. The Colts moved wide receiver Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs in a separate swap as well.

articles.title: “If Things Don’t Go Right”: Jerry Jones Urged to Hire Cowboys Legend & Sooners Coach to Replace Brian Schottenheimer Amid Poor Start
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys are struggling with consistency, discipline, and closing out games in the 2026 season. In the Week 9 game against the Indianapolis Colts,...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are struggling with consistency, discipline, and closing out games in the 2026 season. In the Week 9 game against the Indianapolis Colts , head coach Brian Schottenheimer faced a lot of backlash for the narrow escape with a 27-23 win. It improved their standing with a 4-5 record. But fans and former Cowboys, like Dez Bryant, weren't convinced of Schottenheimer's skills anymore.

According to Bryant, there's one prospect who could perhaps replace Schottenheimer – Jason Witten. The former Cowboys wide receiver urged Cowboys owner Jerry Jones to make the decision and bring Witten in from the Sooners after the latter helped the Oklahoma Sooners to a 23-7 win over the Florida Gators this season.

"I'm sharing this post because of Witten!" Bryant wrote on X , reacting to a clip of Jason Witten reigniting the Sooners' competitive spirit in the locker room. "I'm just saying, @dallascowboys, if things don't go right, you know what to do. ???? ⭐"

This is not the first time Bryant has expressed his hopes of seeing Witten in the Dallas coaching staff. Only a week ago, he posted, "I'm just saying… if anything were to happen in Dallas…Jason Witten should be the next head coach of the Dallas Cowboys. "I can see it..and I'd love that."

It's worth noting that it was Witten's first game as the Sooners' interim offensive coordinator. He brought in a few changes to the format and made practice a bit more professional. Even the players started to appreciate Witten's calls.

Tight end Hayden Hansen claimed that Witten "lit a fire under all of our b–ts." Offensive lineman Michael Fasusi praised Witten's mindset and the knowledge that he brings to practice fields. The best part, according to Fasusi, is that Witten seems like he's happy to be there for the Sooners.

"That's right. Don't flinch. We gotta get better," Witten said in the locker room after the Sooners' latest win. "We gotta practice harder; we gotta practice with more intention, okay? The coaching staff never flinched. The offensive staff, they put their head down and went to work, okay? But don't forget, it's a team. There's big kicks, and there's great defense out there, man. Alright, let it be a lesson for life. Football is a meritocracy. You get what you earn. You guys earned it this week. Let's keep stacking."

The Oklahoma offense showed up big time against Florida. They put up 351 total offensive yards, of which 207 were through the air, and 144 were on the ground. Makes for a nearly balanced offensive attack, something Dallas has struggled with this season. Tight end Rocky Beers tallied an impressive four catches for 72 yards.

Sooners head coach Brent Venables was also impressed with Witten's skills. He certainly believed that the former NFL tight end had the potential to become a full-time coach.

"We spoke about that in the interview process," Venables said about Witten being a potential coordinator in the future. "That's a goal of his. He got started a little later because he was a savage player. One of the best ever. A Hall of Famer. But he's got all of the right stuff. All of the right qualities."

Bringing Jason Witten in as the new head coach could be an easy decision for Jerry Jones. Witten has already spent 16 years in Dallas and played 255 games (started 245 games), caught 1,215 passes for 12,977 yards, and scored 72 touchdowns. He also earned the Pro Bowl nod 11 times in Dallas. He was second in all-time career receiving yards for a tight end in NFL history until Travis Kelce overtook him this season.

Witten witnessed the coaching skills of Bill Parcells, Jason Garrett, and Wade Phillips. Now that he has proven his skills and led the Oklahoma Sooners to a dominating victory, Jones might finally take note of the potential coach.

articles.title: Houston Texans Still Need Another Running Back After Quiet 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: With David Montgomery sidelined and Woody Marks facing an unsustainable workload, Houston’s decision to bypass backfield reinforcements leaves C.J. Stroud vu...
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and the Houston Texans decided to keep their hands in their pockets. No blockbuster deals, no last-minute offensive additions and, most importantly, no additional help in the backfield. While the Texans have shown signs of turning things around, especially following their impressive 44-22 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, I still believe Houston missed an opportunity to address one of its biggest offensive concerns.

Now, before anybody jumps into my mentions, this isn't a knock on Woody Marks or David Montgomery. It's more about having enough ammunition to make it through the second half of the season without putting the entire offensive workload on C.J. Stroud's shoulders.

The Texans Are Gambling on Montgomery's Health

When Houston brought in David Montgomery, the expectation was that he would provide a physical presence in the backfield. A veteran running back who could grind out tough yards, move the chains and give the offense some much-needed balance.

Unfortunately, injuries have thrown a wrench into those plans.

Montgomery has been dealing with a groin injury suffered against the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 11. Head coach DeMeco Ryans described the veteran as week-to-week, and Montgomery remained sidelined against the Chargers.

That's where my concern comes into play.

Groin injuries can be tricky, especially for a running back who relies on explosive cuts, acceleration and fighting through contact. Even when Montgomery returns, there's no guarantee he'll immediately be ready to handle a full workload.

Houston had an opportunity at the trade deadline to give itself a little insurance. Instead, the Texans are betting on Montgomery getting healthy and staying healthy.

That's a pretty big gamble considering how much football is left to play.

Woody Marks Can't Carry the Entire Backfield

Let me be clear: I'm a fan of what Woody Marks brings to this offense.

The young running back has shown flashes of being a legitimate offensive weapon. His ability to contribute as a runner and receiver gives offensive coordinator Nick Caley some flexibility when putting together the game plan.

But there's a difference between being a talented running back and being asked to carry an entire backfield.

The Texans shouldn't have to run Marks into the ground just because Montgomery is unavailable. Houston needs another dependable option who can step in, take meaningful carries and keep the offense moving without a significant drop-off.

Think about it. What happens if Marks takes a hard hit and has to miss a game or two? Suddenly, a backfield that already has injury concerns becomes an even bigger problem.

That's not a situation I want to see the Texans dealing with in December.

Adding another running back wouldn't have been about making a flashy move. It would have been about complementing what this team already does well.

I understand that general manager Nick Caserio isn't going to make a trade just for the sake of making one. Draft capital matters, and overpaying for a rental player isn't necessarily smart business.

However, I have a hard time believing Houston couldn't have explored an affordable option to strengthen its running back room.

The Texans didn't need to go shopping for an All-Pro. A reliable veteran with fresh legs, pass-blocking ability and experience in short-yardage situations could have made a difference.

Now that the deadline has passed, Houston's options are more limited. The Texans can still explore free agents, the waiver wire or other teams' practice squads, but finding an immediate contributor becomes a little more complicated.

The Texans' win over the Chargers was exactly the kind of performance this team needed coming out of the bye week. But one big win shouldn't distract Houston from the holes that still need to be addressed.

I like Montgomery. I like Marks. What I don't like is the idea of Houston entering the most important stretch of the season without another dependable running back in the mix.

The Texans have a defense that can win football games, a franchise quarterback in Stroud and enough offensive talent to make things interesting in the AFC.

So why not give them a little more help?

Houston kept their hands in their pockets at the trade deadline. Now, the front office needs to find another way to reinforce the backfield before an injury or an inconsistent running game makes that decision come back to haunt them.

Because when December football rolls around, you're going to want more than two sets of legs carrying the load.

articles.title: The Chargers Made a Trade, But Should Have Made More
articles.summary: The Chargers traded Daiyan Henley for draft picks but failed to make any other moves at the deadline. With the season lost, Los Angeles missed an opportunity...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers finally decided to make a move before the NFL trade deadline, sending linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. While the return is reasonable for a player in the final year of his contract, the bigger disappointment is that this was the only significant move the Chargers made.

At 0-8 and sitting as the only winless team in the NFL, there really wasn't much reason for the Chargers to stand pat at the deadline. The season has gone about as poorly as possible and the organization should have been looking toward the future. Trading Henley was a step in the right direction, but there were other opportunities to accumulate draft capital that the front office seemingly wasn't willing to pursue.

Henley was an important part of the Chargers defense and losing him isn't going to make things any easier for a team that has already struggled this season. He was a two-time team captain and had 51 tackles through the first eight games. However, with his contract expiring after the season, getting something in return was better than potentially losing him in free agency without receiving anything.

The question is why the Chargers didn't take the same approach with some of their other players.

Khalil Mack immediately comes to mind. Mack is still a productive pass rusher and would have likely attracted interest from several contending teams looking to improve their defense for a playoff run. The Chargers could have potentially received a decent draft pick in exchange for him rather than risk losing him in free agency or bringing him back for another season on a rebuilding roster.

Kimani Vidal is another player the Chargers could have explored trading. Vidal has shown flashes of being a productive running back, but his role has been inconsistent, especially with Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell in the backfield. With the Chargers struggling and looking toward the future, moving Vidal could have made sense if the right offer was available. He is still young and has shown enough potential to attract interest from teams needing help at running back. Rather than potentially letting him walk or keeping him in a limited role, the Chargers could have turned him into another draft asset. Even a Day 3 selection would have been worth considering for a team that needs as many opportunities as possible to improve its roster.

The Chargers don't need to completely tear everything down, but they need to recognize where this season is headed. Sitting at 0-8, the priority should be putting themselves in the best possible position to improve the roster over the next couple of years. That means accumulating draft picks and giving Joe Hortiz as many opportunities as possible to find young talent.

The organization has already shown that it can find contributors through the draft. Adding more selections would only increase those opportunities, whether through making additional picks or using them to move around the draft board.

Ultimately, the Henley trade was a good move considering the circumstances. Getting a fourth-round pick in 2027 and a fifth-round pick in 2028 for a player who was approaching free agency is a reasonable return. However, making just one move at the deadline is difficult to understand given the Chargers' current situation.

There is a difference between trying to remain competitive and refusing to acknowledge when a season is lost. The Chargers needed to start thinking about the future, and the trade for Henley was evidence that they finally recognized that.

Unfortunately, they didn't go far enough. This was an opportunity to add multiple draft assets and give themselves more flexibility heading into the offseason. Instead, the Chargers made one move and called it a day. For a team with an 0-8 record, that simply wasn't enough.

articles.title: Patriots Power Rankings Week 10: Pats join mid-pack mediocrity
articles.summary: Check out where the experts rank the Patriots heading into Week 10
articles.body:
If Dana Carvey's " Church Lady " was a Patriots fan, she surely would have found Sunday's game vs. the Packers "special." It broke records, made history and twisted our insides in ways we hadn't felt in ages, or perhaps ever. So how did the non-fans, the experts take it? Not quite as bad as I thought. The most any expert dropped his ranking was by 5 spots. The fewest was by 1. The average was a slip of 3.5. As a former Patriots philosopher was famous for saying, "It is what it is." Now we can move on.

This week has the Patriots traveling to Germany to play the 6-2 Detroit Lions, who hold second place in the NFC North. That division is on fire and so far New England has an 0-2 (Bears, Packers) against them. It's hard to try and sugarcoat the tough task ahead for the Pats in Week 10. The injured list grew last week and the team will be without two more starters in Ben Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson. The Lions are favored by 2.5 points, which seems low considering the state of the patchwork roster. Frankly, I would be happy to see a good solid effort all around. Hoping for a win, but not feeling too confident unless the offense can limit turnovers and the defense can return to form after a bad week. There's always a chance.

11th – Nate Davis (USA Today): No Patriots team had ever allowed 45 points at Gillette Stadium. No Patriots team had ever allowed 45 points at home … since 1970. And these guys are supposed to be known for their defense . [-1]

It was tempting to pick Week 10 against the Lions in Munich based on how poorly the defense played in a shocking blowout loss to the Packers at home Sunday. But the Patriots are 3-0 in the AFC East, so welcoming Josh Allen & Co. to town could ultimately determine if they still have a shot at the division crown. The Patriots haven't won back-to-back AFC East titles since 2017-18 . — Mike Reiss . [-3]

14th – Frank Schwab (Yahoo! Sports): Christian Gonzalez is a good cornerback who had a horrific game against the Packers. He allowed 105 yards to Matthew Golden and 82 to Christian Watson, according to Next Gen Stats. He's the first player to give up 80 yards to two different players in the same game since at least 2018, according to Next Gen Stats. He had allowed only 196 yards in coverage over his first six games combined, according to NGS . [-3]

14th – Mike Florio (ProFootballTalk): The regression continues . [-4]

14th – Vinnie Iyer (Sporting News): The Patriots, in their five wins, have seen Drake Maye throw a combined two interceptions. In their four losses, he has thrown a combined 9 interceptions. He's starting to press and force the issue in the passing game as the defense keeps struggling, not a good formula . [-4]

15th – Nick Shook (NFL): When Christian Gonzalez — New England's star corner — is getting cooked in coverage to the tune of 10 receptions for 187 yards and a touchdown, per Next Gen Stats, and Drake Maye is throwing three interceptions, we might finally be arriving at a point of agreement: Perhaps these Patriots are just a middling team that could sneak into the playoffs but won't come close to the AFC title run they went on last season . [-4]

15th – Ralph Vacchiano (FOX Sports): We always knew this season was going to be more of a struggle for the defending AFC champions than last season was. The tougher schedule guaranteed that. And while the Patriots secured a big signature win in Buffalo a few weeks ago, they've really fallen flat other than that. They have now played six teams that have winning records and seem likely headed towards the playoffs and they've gone just 2-4 against them. And they looked terrible on Sunday at home against the Packers. That was especially true of QB Drake Maye, who was picked off three times. Stat To Know : The 45 points allowed by the Patriots in Sunday's loss to the Packers are the most points New England has ever allowed in a game at Gillette Stadium (opened in 2002) . [-5]

15th – Conor Orr (SI): I am always fascinated by why a coach will all of a sudden try and pick on one of the best players in the NFL, like the Packers did with Christian Gonzalez on Sunday. What did Matt LaFleur see on film that made him so vulnerable, when Gonzalez had done little but show he was one of the most elite corners in football? [-1]

16th – Ian Glendon (Full Press Coverage): New England was overwhelmed 45-27 by Green Bay, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and absorbing relentless pressure. Injuries to the offensive line and backfield, including Rhamondre Stevenson's knee issue, are making an already uneven offense more fragile. A winning record is no longer enough to protect the Patriots' position . [-4]

articles.title: “That could use my help”: Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus makes big move to rescue Brandon Aiyuk’s NFL career as San Francisco 49ers weigh his future
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk has a way back into the NFL, but it may not come with the San Francisco 49ers.
articles.body: Brandon Aiyuk has a way back into the NFL, but it may not come with the San Francisco 49ers. His new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, expects the wide receiver to play this season and is already preparing for the possibility of finding him on another team.Rosenhaus, who also represents former Miami Dolphins star Tyreek Hill, has helped Aiyuk reconnect with San Francisco and complete the steps needed for reinstatement. However, head coach Kyle Shanahan's latest comments suggest the 49ers have little interest in bringing the receiver back. Drew Rosenhaus prepares to find Brandon Aiyuk a new NFL teamRosenhaus has already made one important move. After taking over Aiyuk's representation, he arranged a meeting between the receiver and the 49ers on November 6. The meeting took place at the team's business offices in Santa Clara, where Aiyuk completed a physical and showed that he was ready to resume his career.The NFL officially reinstated Aiyuk on November 9, giving San Francisco a two-week roster exemption. That period runs until November 23, leaving the 49ers with time to decide whether to keep him, trade him or release him.Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, Rosenhaus explained why he took on Aiyuk's case."I'm in the business of helping players and I felt like this was a player that could use my help. He was in a dilemma, no man's land," the agent said.Rosenhaus also spoke about his relationship with the 49ers, praising head coach Kyle Shanahan, general manager John Lynch and the organisation. He said he used those connections to bring both sides together.However, Shanahan's reaction to Aiyuk's reinstatement offered little hope of a reunion. Speaking to reporters after the NFL's decision, the 49ers coach said, "It means absolutely nothing to our team." He also described the exemption as an administrative matter.Rosenhaus understands the situation and is already preparing for a different outcome."Judging the comments from Coach Shanahan, it doesn't sound like they plan on bringing Brandon back. So when the two weeks is over, it's my job to potentially find a new team for him," he said on The Pat McAfee Show.The agent also confirmed that Aiyuk has been working out independently. He has been running routes and catching footballs, and Rosenhaus is willing to arrange a workout for interested franchises if San Francisco releases him.Tyreek Hill's agent hints at Brandon Aiyuk's potential landing spot amid $13 million disputeRosenhaus has not named a potential destination, but he offered a clue about the kind of franchise that could sign Aiyuk. The agent believes the receiver would benefit from joining a team that already knows his game."I think that in all likelihood Brandon would probably sign with a team that knows him, somebody that has somehow been affiliated with him either in college or the 49ers," Rosenhaus said on The Pat McAfee Show on November 10.That could put franchises with connections to Aiyuk's college career at Arizona State or his time in San Francisco in the conversation. However, Rosenhaus did not confirm any team's interest.There is also a financial issue that could complicate Aiyuk's departure. The 49ers are seeking approximately $13 million in bonus money that the receiver allegedly owes the franchise. San Francisco also voided $27 million in guaranteed money for 2026 after he missed required meetings and team activities during his rehabilitation.Rosenhaus made it clear that the money dispute and Aiyuk's playing future are two separate matters."He hasn't paid anything yet. That's something that we'll work out separately and distinct from the issue of him playing," the agent said on the show.Aiyuk has not played since October 20, 2024, when he suffered ACL and MCL injuries in his right knee against the Kansas City Chiefs. Before that setback, he had enjoyed the best season of his career in 2023, finishing with 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns. He also earned second-team All-Pro honours.Now, Rosenhaus wants to turn that production into another NFL opportunity. With the November 23 deadline approaching, Aiyuk's next move could take him away from San Francisco. The agent believes he can get the receiver back on the field, even if the 49ers are no longer part of the plan.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, might have recorded a pretty impressive performance in the new season so far but his investments have gone for a toss. One of his major investments has been the popular Six Flags Entertainment but it seems the company is now facing billions in debt.Travis Kelce backed Six Flags faces billions in debt as tragic death makes things more and more complicatedAccording to a recent report by the Wall Street Journal, Six Flags is reportedly facing $5 billion in debt as the company is planning to sell off a few parks,A few days ago, Six Flags CEO John Reilly reflected on the company as he spoke to investors and said how the company is looking toward “optimizing the portfolio” as he added “We carry more debt than we want…bringing it down is a priority…”Six Flags CEO John Reilly added, “We are actively reviewing our parks and real estate, including potential sales of non-core assets, to unlock value, reduce debt, and enhance liquidity.”For now, it has not been confirmed which park Six Flags have been planning to sell off.While Six Flags' profits have been a topic of concern since 2024, the recent tragic death at their park in Georgia has complicated things for him.Six Flags’ profit takes a hit amid 42 year old man being ejected from rollercoaster and falling to his deathFor the unversed, last month, a 42 year old school teacher from Atlanta, Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, was ejected from his seat while riding the infamous Goliath and fell to his death.This led to the Goliath’s closure in at least 10 parks across the country which has only made things more and more complicated for Six Flags.Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem’s death has devastated communities in Atlanta as many have expressed their anger towards Six Flags Entertainment.Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem’s school issued a statement about his death which read as, "The Wesley International Academy community is devastated by the loss of Hassan Kariem, affectionately known as Mr. Kariem, who was a beloved colleague, friend, and integral part of the Wesley family for more than 12 years…”The statement added, “His love for Wesley, dedication to our students, and commitment to our school community were evident in everything he did. Mr. Kariem was deeply loved and respected, and his absence will be felt throughout our school community. Our hearts are with his family, friends, colleagues, students, and all who knew and loved him as we mourn this tremendous loss. We ask that our community keep Mr. Kariem's family in their thoughts and respect their privacy during this difficult time."Despite the anger, Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem’s family has not issued a statement yet.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WTGL debut match draws nearly 100,000 viewers going against NFL
articles.summary: WTGL's inaugural match, televised by ESPN, drew an average of 97,000 viewers at SoFi Center, peaking at 138,000. The Nov. 8 match went head-to-head with the...
articles.body:
WTGL had plenty of competition for its Nov. 8 debut, going up against the NFL, the men's golf World Wide Technology Championship televised by Golf Channel and NASCAR.

The match, televised by ESPN, drew an average of 97,000 viewers at SoFi Center, peaking at 138,000. The WWT, which featured a playoff between Blades Brown and Ben James, had an average viewership of 110,00. Brown and James are playing this season for TGL.

WTGL's inaugural match — in which Los Angeles Golf Club defeated New York Golf Club , 3-1 — delivered the third highest women's golf telecast out of 24 events since the Sept. 13 Solheim Cup .

The league's second match, Tuesday, Nov. 10, was televised by ION.

The WTGL format follows TGL, the men's version co-founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, that is entering its third year.

The initial match was a success with the players.

"Witnessing LPGA players and LPGA stars in this format is so different," said LA's Michelle Wie West. "We have such amazing players and personalities out on Tour, and it's really cool that every single shot you see so many statistics on the screen. I think that's something that's missing from our normal broadcast. I think for two hours, LPGA fans, existing fans, can witness our players in a whole different light, and I think we'll attract new fans as well too."

Tom D'Angelo is a senior sports columnist and reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at tdangelo@pbpost.com.

articles.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
articles.summary: Senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti, one of Oregon's top pass rushers with 5.5 sacks, will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a knee injury agai...
articles.body:
EUGENE — One of Oregon football's most important defensive players is done for the season.

Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon's 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday.

"Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he's been here," Lanning said. "Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum's done for the year, he had a knee injury, he'll end up having surgery."

Tuioti was among the Ducks' leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front.

In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game.

"I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on," Lanning said. "He left it on the line there on the field, and I don't know if he'll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky."

Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts.
